- Helper: src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts - Template and story path: const STORY_PATH = "docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md"; const ANNOTATION = `/** @story ${STORY_PATH} */`; - hasStoryAnnotation(...) checks JSDoc, leading comments, ancestor comments, and surrounding text to avoid duplicate annotations. - reportMissing(...) (annotated with @story 008.0 and @req REQ-AUTOFIX-MISSING) reports missing @story and provides both fix and suggest using createAddStoryFix(resolvedTarget). - reportMethod(...) does the same for methods/interfaces using createMethodFix. - Both are wrapped in try/catch, so in edge cases they quietly skip fixing rather than breaking ESLint (safe failure mode).
- Core fix logic: src/rules/helpers/require-story-core.ts - createAddStoryFix(target): • Computes insertion offset from target.range or its export parent. • Returns fixer.insertTextBeforeRange([start, start], `${ANNOTATION}\n`). • Only adds a single-line JSDoc comment above the function; does not alter any executable code. - createMethodFix(node): similar, but inserts `${ANNOTATION}\n ` to align indentation for methods. - These satisfy: • REQ-AUTOFIX-MISSING: automatically add @story to functions/methods. • REQ-AUTOFIX-SAFE: only comments are added, runtime code untouched. • REQ-AUTOFIX-PRESERVE: change is minimal and based on ranges, preserving surrounding formatting.
4) Implementation: @story path format auto-fix (REQ-AUTOFIX-FORMAT / REQ-AUTOFIX-SAFE / REQ-AUTOFIX-PRESERVE) - Rule: src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts - Multiple JSDoc blocks reference docs/stories/008.0-DEV-AUTO-FIX.story.md and @req REQ-AUTOFIX-FORMAT, REQ-AUTOFIX-SAFE, REQ-AUTOFIX-PRESERVE. - meta.fixable is restricted to safe suffix normalization: meta: { ..., /** This rule's fixable support is limited to safe @story path suffix normalization per Story 008.0 ... */ fixable: "code", }
- createStoryFix(context, comment, fixed): - Reads full comment text; locates "@story" and captures only its value substring using indices + regex. - Returns null when the tag or value range cannot be reliably determined (TAG_NOT_FOUND_INDEX or failed match). - When successful, computes precise [start,end] range inside comment.range and returns a function that applies fixer.replaceTextRange(fixRange, fixed). - This ensures only the @story path substring is changed; all other text/whitespace remains exactly as-is.
- reportInvalidStoryFormatWithFix(...): - Calls createStoryFix; if it returns null, falls back to plain reportInvalidStoryFormat (no fix), explicitly annotated as REQ-AUTOFIX-SAFE. - If a fix is available, calls context.report with messageId "invalidStoryFormat" and fix: fixFactory().
- validateStoryAnnotation(...): - Collapses and validates the path against options.storyPattern. - If whitespace or other invalid structure: reportInvalidStoryFormat (no fix). - Otherwise: const fixed = getFixedStoryPath(collapsed); if (fixed && pathPattern.test(fixed)) { reportInvalidStoryFormatWithFix(...); return; } // else, just report without fix - Satisfies REQ-AUTOFIX-FORMAT (suffix-only auto-fix) and REQ-AUTOFIX-SAFE/PRESERVE (only safe, pattern-compliant fixes applied; others are reported only).
- Behavior is exactly what auto-fix tests assert in tests/rules/auto-fix-behavior-008.test.ts for REQ-AUTOFIX-FORMAT (adding .md or .story.md suffixes and leaving valid paths unchanged).
5) Documentation of auto-fix capabilities (AC: Documentation) - File: user-docs/api-reference.md - Section: traceability/require-story-annotation • Documents that when run with --fix the rule inserts a single-line placeholder JSDoc @story above missing functions, methods, TS declare functions, and interface method signatures. • States template is currently fixed but structured for future configurability. • Confirms fixes are strictly limited to adding the placeholder annotation without altering function body or runtime behavior. - Section: traceability/valid-annotation-format • States that --fix is limited to safe @story path suffix normalization (e.g., add .md when path ends with .story, or add .story.md when there is no extension). • Confirms it does not change directories, infer new story names, or modify surrounding comment text/whitespace. • Notes that more advanced path normalization and selective toggles are planned but not yet implemented.
6) Requirements explicitly marked as future (non-blocking for this story) - REQ-AUTOFIX-TEMPLATE and REQ-AUTOFIX-SELECTIVE are clearly noted in the story as "Not yet implemented" and described as future enhancements. - Current implementation and docs match that: templates are fixed, and selective enabling/disabling beyond normal ESLint rule configuration is not yet present. - Acceptance criteria in the story treat these as future work, not required for this iteration, so their absence does not contradict any checked criterion.
traceability.notes: Story 008.0-DEV-AUTO-FIX is fully implemented. The require-story-annotation rule provides ESLint auto-fix for missing @story annotations on functions and methods via meta.fixable="code" and the createAddStoryFix/createMethodFix helpers, guarded by hasStoryAnnotation checks and try/catch to ensure safety and formatting preservation. The valid-annotation-format rule provides narrowly scoped, suffix-only @story path normalization using getFixedStoryPath and createStoryFix, with explicit fallbacks to reporting-only behavior when a safe fix cannot be determined. Dedicated tests in tests/rules/auto-fix-behavior-008.test.ts directly reference this story and its REQ-AUTOFIX-MISSING and REQ-AUTOFIX-FORMAT requirements and pass as part of the Jest test suite. User documentation in user-docs/api-reference.md accurately describes what --fix does for both rules and the safety constraints, matching the story’s documentation acceptance criterion. Future-focused requirements (configurable templates and selective fix toggles) are explicitly out of scope in the story and are correctly not implemented yet. Therefore, all in-scope acceptance criteria and requirements for this story are satisfied.
